eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Nine
subtitle: Lesson 111 · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

eyebrow: Ordinary blocking resolves itself. This doesn't.
code:
-- Blocking: B waits for A -- then A commits -- B proceeds.
-- Deadlock: A waits for B, AND B waits for A.
-- Neither ever releases first. No way out alone.
caption: A genuine cycle, not just a wait.

code:
-- Session A: holds X on Product 680, WANTS Product 681
UPDATE ... WHERE ProductID = 680;  -- held
UPDATE ... WHERE ProductID = 681;  -- wants, blocked

-- Session B: holds X on Product 681, WANTS Product 680
UPDATE ... WHERE ProductID = 681;  -- held
UPDATE ... WHERE ProductID = 680;  -- wants, blocked
caption: A holds what B wants. B holds what A wants. Cycle complete.

eyebrow: The deadlock monitor breaks the cycle
code:
-- A background process checks the lock graph
-- for cycles like this one.
-- Found -> picks a VICTIM -> kills it -> rolls it back
caption: Rolling back the victim releases its locks, freeing the other side.

code:
-- Msg 1205: Transaction (Process ID n) was deadlocked on
-- lock resources with another process and has been chosen
-- as the deadlock victim. Rerun the transaction.
caption: Expected, not exceptional — and retrying is the standard response.

subtitle: Seeing exactly what happened, after the fact.
